headline: High: shared networked research workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance gaps are plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter ingests external web/API content via OpenAI, Exa, and Tavily, while gpt-researcher also fetches web content and can use MCP. If dexter outputs are fed into gpt-researcher, attacker-controlled text can become instructions. The pair has a plausible shared content bridge, though no direct interaction evidence is provided.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are copied into gpt-researcher prompts or MCP inputs
IF gpt-researcher processes untrusted web text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt template
Strip HTML/markdown before passing content between agents
Require provenance tags on all imported snippets
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends content to multiple APIs. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive material can flow from A into B and then to third-party services. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is inferred and escalated for uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or document set
IF dexter places financial data into files that gpt-researcher uploads to external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove sensitive files before running gpt-researcher
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Use redacted copies of source documents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress plus API access, so they can contend over shared mutable resources if co-located. dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and gpt-researcher reads/writes local documents and can spawn subprocesses. No locking is documented, so overlapping writes are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree
IF either agent writes to shared scratch or output files without locks
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
Keep separate API credential files
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher pipeline, so it can treat upstream material as authoritative and then publish it. dexter produces research outputs from APIs and web sources; if those outputs are fed into gpt-researcher without verification, errors or fabricated claims can cascade into published reports or actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are used as source material for gpt-researcher reports
IF gpt-researcher publishes or acts on those outputs without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before publishing
Cross-check claims against original sources
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted inputs
Disable auto-publish for paired runs
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and broad external API calls. If regulated financial or personal data is placed into gpt-researcher, retention and residency obligations may differ from dexter's workflow. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a cautious medium finding.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is included in gpt-researcher inputs
IF the deployment requires retention or residency controls not enforced by both agents
mitigations: Classify and exclude regulated data from paired runs
Review vendor retention settings before use
Use anonymized or synthetic datasets
Log data flows for compliance review
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
